aliases: Fe-17%Al monocrystal with 70 ppm C after 14 days at 320 °C with 100 MPa loading

summary: A Bridgman-grown Fe-17%Al single crystal (real composition 16.8 at.% Al, 8.9 wt.-%, with 70 wt.ppm C) that was annealed for 14 days at 320 °C under a concurrent 100 MPa load applied along the <111> direction. Within the study of the low-temperature deformation behaviour of iron-rich Fe-Al alloys, this sample is notable as the only monocrystal in which thin carbides precipitated in the bulk after the mechanically loaded heat treatment, whereas the same treatment without loading produced much less carbide. The research question addressed is how heat treatment, applied stress, Al content and quenched-in excess vacancies—rather than short-range ordering—control the strength and ductility of low-carbon Fe-Al alloys.
composition: Binary Fe-17%Al alloy (nominal 17 at.% Al). The real composition of this monocrystal was determined as 16.8 at.% Al (8.9 wt.-%), with impurity contents of 70 wt.ppm C, 140 wt.ppm Si, 50 wt.ppm Cu and 90 wt.ppm Mo. The base metal was Fe of 99.99% purity, purified by zone melting to minimise impurities, and Al of 99.999% purity; all alloys of the study were kept below 100 wt.ppm C by design. The low, unavoidable carbon level (70 wt.ppm) is the origin of the thin carbides that precipitate during the subsequent heat treatment, while the low overall impurity level is intended to isolate intrinsic solid-solution and ordering effects from carbide or segregation effects.
